items.title: Write River Wend environment concepts prompts (5 assets)
items.description:
## Why
The River Wend links Briar Glen to the sea and adds three class-route set pieces (Stone Stair, Millweir, Weeping Adit) plus the towpath and Kestrel Lock; they need a shared look before any river asset is made (style bible §2.2 River Wend row).

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/environment/<asset-id>.md` (category: environment) from template `environment-concept.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Briar Glen Quay with the stone barge *Patient Ann* (ochre hull stripe, no painted name) taking on dressed glenstone blocks from their timber cradles, a quay crane, and the Stone Stair, a stepped slipway for blocks coming down from the Deepworks' cutting hall, pale with stone dust; the Vesperine Millweir with a bell-mark keystone, clear walkable sluice top and two water levels; the Weeping Adit mouth where the Wend springs from the hill (cold, dripping, a faint Nightjar shimmer #CFC6F2 on the water), flooded tunnel with air pockets and an empty stone barge being winched back up on its chain; the towpath down the valley; Kestrel Lock with balance-beam gates, windlasses, a flaking toll board (no legible text) and Old Reed's cottage.

Asset ids (5):
- `env-briar-glen-quay-01`
- `env-millweir-sluice-walk-01`
- `env-weeping-adit-mouth-01`
- `env-towpath-valley-01`
- `env-kestrel-lock-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-env-river-concepts-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

## Notes
Water is standing water only (no flowing-river sim); the barge ride is a narrated card (`e37-asset-barge-ride-cards-*`), so `env-barge-ride-card-01` from the needs list is produced there as runtime key art.

Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock` as reference inputs. Canon names and details follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 5 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble block with docs/art/style-bible.md §14, then it matches byte-for-byte and the correct §14.1 category add-on follows it.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it names its consuming bead(s), output spec (16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture) and the filled consistency checklist, with no unfilled `<…>` placeholders.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt writes out the palette hexes, shape language and silhouette rules needed to meet the approval criterion: each painting sits in the River Wend palette (brown water #6B5A3E, reeds #8FA05A, tarred timber #3A2E26, lock-gate red #A8473A), water reads as water but not as a current, and every class route (climb the Stone Stair, walk the sluice top, swim the Adit air pockets) is visible.
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that asks for text/letters, names an artist, studio or game, uses a non-canon name for a story-bible subject, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails and names the file and line.

items.title: Generate River Wend environment concepts via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 5 prompt files of `e37-asset-env-river-concepts-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-env-river-concepts-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 5 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (16:9, 1536×864 generate, PNG, painterly concept — reference/mood target for grey-box and art-dress, not a runtime texture), then dimensions, transparency/background and layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

items.title: Owner approval: River Wend environment concepts
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the image gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the batch review page of 5 candidates and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: image, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-env-river-concepts-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: each painting sits in the River Wend palette (brown water #6B5A3E, reeds #8FA05A, tarred timber #3A2E26, lock-gate red #A8473A), water reads as water but not as a current, and every class route (climb the Stone Stair, walk the sluice top, swim the Adit air pockets) is visible. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.

items.title: Write Saltmarch weapon, arrow and tool SFX prompts (12 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Imported gear must sound foreign and its gameplay-relevant noise must match the sim: a whistling arrow is a lure, glass shatter tears Hushlings, glue-soled boots are quieter than any gait.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset (or round-robin set) in `assets/prompts/sfx/<asset-id>.md` from `_templates/sfx.md`, with the SFX PREAMBLE (audio bible §8) verbatim, the category add-on, sourcing (generated vs CC0), round-robin count, sim link, output spec and checklist.

Saltmarch sabre ring (thinner, higher than local steel), harpoon-spear haft thrum, sharkskin brigandine rasp layer (quieter than leather), arrows: whistling shriek, netting thwump, tar slap, glass-headed shatter, grapple clink and pay-out; Undertow tools: smoke pearl pop-hiss, glue-soled boot peel, skeleton-key ring jingle, tide-silk rope whisper.

Asset ids (12):
- `sfx-saltmarch-sabre-ring-01`
- `sfx-harpoon-spear-thrum-01`
- `sfx-armor-sharkskin-layer`
- `sfx-arrow-whistling-01`
- `sfx-arrow-netting-01`
- `sfx-arrow-tar-01`
- `sfx-arrow-glass-shatter-01`
- `sfx-arrow-grapple-01`
- `sfx-smoke-pearl-01`
- `sfx-glue-boots-peel-01`
- `sfx-key-ring-jingle-01`
- `sfx-tide-silk-rope-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Sim link (surface id / noise radius / creature state / world fact) per sound
- Out: Generation (`e38-asset-sfx-saltmarch-imports-generate`)

## Notes
Ids follow part A patterns (`sfx-armor-<material>-layer`, `sfx-arrow-*`). No duplicates of part A arrow or armour sounds.

Prompts cite the locked reference sounds from `e38-asset-sonic-lock`. Canon names follow `docs/narrative/story-bible.md`; no intelligible speech anywhere (text-only MVP).
